package_info.why_malicious: The plugin generates and displays a fake ransomware notice on WordPress sites, attempting to extort website owners by demanding payment for file recovery, despite no actual encryption occurring. This is a clear case of social engineering and extortion via malicious code.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Your website has been encrypted!

To recover your files, send 0.1 bitcoin to the following address...
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code generates and serves a ransom note HTML page, displaying a fake message about file encryption and demanding payment, with no actual encryption performed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Displaying a ransom note without any legitimate administrative action is a clear sign of malicious intent, especially when no files are actually encrypted.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate WordPress plugin should not generate or display ransom/extortion messages to site owners.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate maintenance or warning banners may be displayed by plugins, but never for extortion or false claims.

attack_chain.action: Attacker deploys a bogus WordPress plugin to target websites.
Plugin generates and serves a fake ransomware HTML page to site owners.
attack_chain.leads_to: Site owners see the ransom note and may be tricked into paying.

behavioral_signatures: WordPress plugin generating and serving ransom note HTML pages
Display of extortion messages without actual file encryption
Sudden appearance of new HTML files with ransom content
file_indicators: HTML files containing phrases like 'Your website has been encrypted!'
Unusual plugin directories or files not matching known legitimate plugins
network_indicators: No direct network indicators unless payment address is checked or plugin phones home
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified HTML files in the WordPress root or plugin directories containing ransom/extortion language. Flag plugins that generate or serve such content. Correlate with lack of actual file encryption activity to identify fake ransomware attempts.
